Community Health Council — Quarterly Clinical Study Record
Record ID: CHC-Q2-0426 | Date: 2026-04-15 | Source: Media IT System
Patient group: Adult asthma patients, mean age 34.7 years
Objective: To evaluate efficacy of inhaled budesonide in reducing exacerbation frequency over three months.
Methods: A total of 112 patients diagnosed with moderate persistent asthma received 400 mcg budesonide twice daily. Peak expiratory flow rates (PEFR) were monitored weekly, alongside patient-reported symptom scores and rescue inhaler usage.
Results: Mean PEFR improved from 280 L/min before treatment to 340 L/min post-treatment indicating enhanced airway function. Frequency of exacerbations decreased by 38% (p < 0.05). Compliance rate averaged 91%. No serious adverse effects reported.
Conclusion: Inhaled budesonide demonstrates significant benefit for asthma control in adults, supporting its continued use in community health management programs.
Notes: This record is a routine quarterly summary generated from clinical data exports (MEDSYS) and intended for clinician review. Billing information and patient identifiers are omitted for privacy.

Cook Time: 45 minutes

- 900 g pumpkin purée
- 500 ml vegetable broth
- 200 ml heavy cream
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 15 ml olive oil
- 5 g ground nutmeg
- 2 g freshly ground black pepper
- 5 g kosher salt

For preparation, heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until translucent, approximately 5 minutes. Add pumpkin purée and vegetable broth, then stir to combine thoroughly. Bring mixture to a simmer, reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 40 minutes.
